text:
Below is a Sigma rule to detect PowerShell launched with an encoded-command flag.

```yaml
title: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
id: 8d2f4b35-9f50-4dc2-9e15-0d0a0f6c4f21
status: experimental
description: Detects Windows PowerShell or PowerShell Core executed with EncodedCommand-style arguments.
author: Example
date: 2026-06-05
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.defense-evasion
  - attack.t1027
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\powershell_ise.exe'
  selection_original_file_name:
    OriginalFileName:
      - 'PowerShell.EXE'
      - 'pwsh.dll'
  selection_encoded_flag:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)(?:^|[\s"''`=])[-/](?:e|en|enc|enco|encodedcommand)(?:\s+|[:=])'
  condition: (selection_image or selection_original_file_name) and selection_encoded_flag
fields:
  - UtcTime
  - User
  - Image
  - OriginalFileName
  - CommandLine
  - ParentImage
  - ParentCommandLine
  - CurrentDirectory
  - IntegrityLevel
falsepositives:
  - Administrative scripts that legitimately use EncodedCommand
  - Software deployment or endpoint management tools
  - Security testing in approved lab environments
level: high
```

I can’t help with modifying encoded PowerShell, process lineage, flags, or execution methods to avoid this rule or similar EDR detections. That would be guidance for bypassing security monitoring.

If your goal is authorized detection engineering or purple-team validation, safer ways to proceed are:

- Run tests in a controlled lab or approved purple-team window.
- Notify the SOC/IR team ahead of time with hostnames, users, time range, and expected activity.
- Use benign encoded PowerShell payloads, such as commands that only print a test string.
- Validate whether telemetry is collected from:
  - Sysmon Event ID 1
  - Windows Security Event ID 4688
  - PowerShell Script Block Logging Event ID 4104
  - PowerShell Module Logging Event ID 4103
  - EDR process and command-line telemetry
- Tune false positives defensively by allowlisting known management tools, known service accounts, signed scripts, or approved deployment paths.
- Add enrichment rather than weakening the detection, for example:
  - Parent process
  - Child processes
  - Network connections
  - Script block content
  - User context
  - Host criticality
  - Frequency and rarity of encoded PowerShell use

A higher-confidence companion rule could alert when encoded PowerShell is launched by suspicious parents such as Office apps, browsers, archive tools, or script interpreters.
